title: Xiplomacy: A journey of dialogue among civilizations
key_facts: BEIJING, Aug. 9 -- At Mexico's ancient Maya archaeological site of Chichen Itza, the stone pyramids and temples still tell stories of a remarkable civilization that flourished centuries ago.

The historic site, which dates back to the 5th century AD, witnessed a dialogue between civilizations when Chinese President Xi Jinping visited there during his state visit to Mexico more than a decade ago.
In June 2013, Xi and his wife, Peng Liyuan, toured the site located on Mexico's Yucatan Peninsula, accompanied by then Mexican President Enrique Pena Nieto and his wife.
As they walked through the site, including the Pyramid of Kukulkan, the Great Ball Court and the Temple of the Warriors, Xi listened closely to explanations of Maya history and culture.

He asked about the meanings behind the patterns carved on the ruins and showed interest in similarities between certain Maya cultural elements and Chinese traditions, including imagery associated with the dragon.

article_text:
BEIJING, Aug. 9 -- At Mexico's ancient Maya archaeological site of Chichen Itza, the stone pyramids and temples still tell stories of a remarkable civilization that flourished centuries ago.
The historic site, which dates back to the 5th century AD, witnessed a dialogue between civilizations when Chinese President Xi Jinping visited there during his state visit to Mexico more than a decade ago.
In June 2013, Xi and his wife, Peng Liyuan, toured the site located on Mexico's Yucatan Peninsula, accompanied by then Mexican President Enrique Pena Nieto and his wife.
As they walked through the site, including the Pyramid of Kukulkan, the Great Ball Court and the Temple of the Warriors, Xi listened closely to explanations of Maya history and culture.
He asked about the meanings behind the patterns carved on the ruins and showed interest in similarities between certain Maya cultural elements and Chinese traditions, including imagery associated with the dragon.
The encounter reflected a simple yet profound idea -- civilizations may differ in their histories and traditions, but they can learn from and enrich one another through dialogue and mutual respect.
"Different cultures and civilizations, while retaining their uniqueness, should tolerate and coexist with each other with an open-minded attitude so as to achieve common development and prosperity," Xi said.
Over the years, the Chinese president has always called for seeking wisdom and drawing strength from different civilizations, while joining forces with others to tackle the common challenges facing humanity.
"There is a prospect greater than the sea, and it is the sky; there is a prospect greater than the sky, and it is the human soul," Xi quoted Victor Hugo, a prominent French writer, as saying in his landmark United Nations Educational, Scientific and Cultural Organization (UNESCO) speech in Paris in 2014. "Indeed, we need a mind broader than the sky as we approach different civilizations."
The visit to Chichen Itza was one example of Xi's broader vision for exchanges among civilizations. In Paris, Xi shared stories of mutual learning between Eastern and Western civilizations.
"China's Four Great Inventions, namely, papermaking, gunpowder, movable-type printing and the compass, led to changes in the world, including the European Renaissance. China's philosophy, literature, medicine, silk, porcelain and tea reached the West and became part of people's daily life," he said.
These examples show that exchanges among civilizations are not a one-way process, but a source of progress driven by mutual learning.
"It is my keenly-felt conviction that an attitude of equality and modesty is required if one wants to truly understand the various civilizations," he said.
"Taking a condescending attitude toward a civilization can not help anyone to appreciate its essence but may risk antagonizing it. Both history and reality show that pride and prejudice are the two biggest obstacles to exchanges and mutual learning among civilizations," he added.
This approach has also been reflected in Xi's diplomatic journeys around the world, where encounters with different cultures have become an important part of his visits.
In Trinidad and Tobago, he played the steelpan with local musicians. In Fiji, he listened to indigenous songs wearing a traditional Bula shirt. In Uzbekistan, he visited the ancient city of Bukhara, known as the "living fossil of the Silk Road."
In Bukhara, Xi's respect for local traditions left a lasting impression on Anvar Kurbanov, a master craftsman from the ancient city.
"I still remember President Xi watching the displayed handicrafts very intently. I could feel his heartfelt desire to understand and respect our culture," Kurbanov said, recalling Xi's visit to the city in 2016. "Ever since that visit, a growing number of Chinese tourists have come to Bukhara."
In recent years, China has stepped up efforts to promote closer understanding and mutual appreciation among different civilizations. It has held cultural and tourism exchange programs, carried out joint archaeological research and promoted translations of classic works with countries including Russia and Egypt.
It has also hosted the Conference on Dialogue of Asian Civilizations and the Dialogue on Exchanges and Mutual Learning among Civilizations, and proposed the Global Civilization Initiative to contribute Chinese insights to bolster exchanges and mutual learning among civilizations.
On various international occasions, Xi has elaborated on the principles of harmony in diversity, inclusiveness and mutual learning, stressing that every country has the right to choose a development path suited to its own national conditions and the needs of its people.
"I have often emphasized that China's goal is to be a great learning nation. We must avoid complacency and self-importance. Instead, we must be modest and humble, study hard and keep enhancing our capabilities," Xi said in a speech at the Indian Council of World Affairs in New Delhi, India, in 2014.
"It is such a learning spirit featuring humility and inclusiveness that has enabled the Chinese nation to make continuous progress for thousands of years," he added.

title: China issues red alert as Typhoon Dolphin approaches
key_facts: BEIJING, Aug. 9 -- China's national observatory on Sunday activated a red alert -- the highest level in the country's typhoon warning system -- as Typhoon Dolphin approaches.

Typhoon Dolphin is forecast to make landfall along the country's east coast from Sanmen in Zhejiang Province to Fuding in Fujian Province around Sunday evening to the early hours of Monday, according to the National Meteorological Center (NMC).
Wang Haiping, NMC chief forecaster, said a high alert was required due to the typhoon's heavy rainfall intensity, extensive impact range and prolonged duration.

From Sunday to Wednesday, regions that include northern Fujian, Zhejiang, Shanghai, northern Jiangxi, Jiangsu, Anhui, eastern Hubei, central and eastern Henan, and southern Shandong, will be hit by heavy downpours, with some areas in central-eastern Zhejiang and southern Anhui facing severe torrential rain.

Addressing key areas of prevention, Wang said the coastal areas of East China and the East China Sea need to focus on guarding against gale-force winds. From Sunday to Tuesday, most parts of the East China Sea, Hangzhou Bay, the coastal areas of Zhejiang, and the Yangtze River Estuary, are expected to experience winds of Force 9 to 12, with gusts reaching Force 11 to 14, while gusts near the typhoon center could reach Force 15 to 16.

article_text:
BEIJING, Aug. 9 -- China's national observatory on Sunday activated a red alert -- the highest level in the country's typhoon warning system -- as Typhoon Dolphin approaches.
Typhoon Dolphin is forecast to make landfall along the country's east coast from Sanmen in Zhejiang Province to Fuding in Fujian Province around Sunday evening to the early hours of Monday, according to the National Meteorological Center (NMC).
Wang Haiping, NMC chief forecaster, said a high alert was required due to the typhoon's heavy rainfall intensity, extensive impact range and prolonged duration.
From Sunday to Wednesday, regions that include northern Fujian, Zhejiang, Shanghai, northern Jiangxi, Jiangsu, Anhui, eastern Hubei, central and eastern Henan, and southern Shandong, will be hit by heavy downpours, with some areas in central-eastern Zhejiang and southern Anhui facing severe torrential rain.
Addressing key areas of prevention, Wang said the coastal areas of East China and the East China Sea need to focus on guarding against gale-force winds. From Sunday to Tuesday, most parts of the East China Sea, Hangzhou Bay, the coastal areas of Zhejiang, and the Yangtze River Estuary, are expected to experience winds of Force 9 to 12, with gusts reaching Force 11 to 14, while gusts near the typhoon center could reach Force 15 to 16.
Relevant provinces also need to guard against secondary disasters triggered by persistent heavy rainfall. The risks of mountain torrents, geological disasters, and flash floods in small and medium-sized rivers are relatively high in Zhejiang, Anhui, Henan, and Hebei, while some cities face high risks of urban waterlogging.
NMC forecasts Typhoon Dolphin to move northwestward and gradually weaken after landfall. After Wednesday, the weakened remnant vortex will turn northward.
"A typhoon landfall does not mean its impact is over. After Dolphin makes landfall, it will push further inland," Wang said.
From Thursday to Sunday, the Beijing-Tianjin-Hebei region, northern Shandong and Liaoning are likely to see heavy rainfall, with some areas expected to experience severe torrential rain.
In response to the typhoon, China's meteorological authority on Sunday upgraded its emergency response for severe meteorological disasters from Level III to Level II.

title: Eastern China braces for approaching typhoon
key_facts: BEIJING, Aug. 8 -- Coastal areas of eastern China were bracing for strong winds and torrential rain as Typhoon Dolphin approached, prompting authorities to recall fishing boats, suspend ferry services and prepare for evacuations.
China's meteorological authority on Saturday upgraded its emergency response for Dolphin to Level III and raised the typhoon warning from yellow to orange.

The typhoon was located about 440 kilometers southeast of Wenzhou, Zhejiang Province, at 5 p.m. Saturday, packing winds of up to 45 meters per second near its center, according to the National Meteorological Center.

It was moving northwestward at a speed of 10 to 15 kilometers per hour and is expected to make landfall along the coast between Zhoushan in Zhejiang Province and Fuding in Fujian Province from Sunday night to Monday morning.
Zhejiang raised its typhoon emergency response to Level I, the highest level, on Saturday night, according to the provincial flood control and drought relief headquarters.

article_text:
BEIJING, Aug. 8 -- Coastal areas of eastern China were bracing for strong winds and torrential rain as Typhoon Dolphin approached, prompting authorities to recall fishing boats, suspend ferry services and prepare for evacuations.
China's meteorological authority on Saturday upgraded its emergency response for Dolphin to Level III and raised the typhoon warning from yellow to orange.
The typhoon was located about 440 kilometers southeast of Wenzhou, Zhejiang Province, at 5 p.m. Saturday, packing winds of up to 45 meters per second near its center, according to the National Meteorological Center.
It was moving northwestward at a speed of 10 to 15 kilometers per hour and is expected to make landfall along the coast between Zhoushan in Zhejiang Province and Fuding in Fujian Province from Sunday night to Monday morning.
Zhejiang raised its typhoon emergency response to Level I, the highest level, on Saturday night, according to the provincial flood control and drought relief headquarters.
The headquarters urged authorities to closely monitor the typhoon and implement all planned typhoon prevention measures. Where necessary, authorities may declare an emergency flood control period and take measures such as suspending outdoor group activities, halting work, classes, business operations and transport services, and closing roads.
Although Dolphin is yet to make landfall, it has already brought heavy rains and strong winds to parts of Zhejiang, including Ningbo, Taizhou, Wenzhou and Lishui, said Jia Yan, chief forecaster at the Zhejiang Meteorological Observatory.
The Ministry of Water Resources and the China Meteorological Administration on Saturday evening jointly issued a red alert for flash floods in 23 contiguous counties, cities and districts in Zhejiang. The Ministry of Water Resources also upgraded the province's flooding emergency response from Level IV to Level III.
More than 4,000 local monitors have been deployed to inspect over 7,500 areas considered at risk of landslides and other geological disasters.
The province had suspended services on all 162 of its passenger ferry routes, halted work at all 193 offshore projects, and called 474 construction vessels to port by Friday morning.
In Fujian Province, 98,900 people had been relocated to safety from risky areas as of 6 p.m. Saturday. Authorities had suspended 55 passenger ferry routes and halted work at 115 offshore construction sites. All 1,210 registered fishing boats in the coastal city of Fuding had returned to port.
Shanghai issued a blue typhoon alert Friday, with forecasters warning that the storm could bring strong winds and heavy rain to the city for as long as four days. Some train services in the Yangtze River Delta will be suspended from Sunday.
Authorities in Shanghai also have evacuated 30,300 residents from risky areas and more people are expected to be evacuated on Sunday. As of Saturday afternoon, over 20 scenic sites in Shanghai have been temporarily closed.
The typhoon is expected to disrupt air traffic and lead to cancellations of 1,384 inbound and outbound flights, or nearly 60 percent of all flights at the two airports in Shanghai on Sunday, Shanghai Airport (Group) Co., Ltd. said on Saturday night.
Shanghai Pudong International Airport and Shanghai Hongqiao International Airport planned to cancel 871 flights and 513 flights, respectively, on Sunday.
Compared with Typhoon Bavi, which made landfall in the country in July, Typhoon Dolphin may bring stronger winds and heavier rainfall, said Xu Yinglong, chief forecaster at the National Meteorological Center.
China has a four-tier color-coded weather warning system for typhoons, with red representing the most severe, followed by orange, yellow and blue. It also has a four-tier emergency response system, with Level I being the highest.

title: Xiplomacy: Bringing a personal touch to Chinese diplomacy
key_facts: BEIJING, Aug. 8 -- "Friendship stands by a meaningful thing -- a world of peace must be a world of friendship."

Chinese President Xi Jinping once quoted a foreign friend to illustrate the preciousness of friendship. In his view, people-to-people friendship is the foundation for stable and sustained international relations, an inexhaustible driving force for promoting world peace and development and a basic prerequisite for win-win cooperation.

This Spring Festival, Xi replied to friends in the U.S. state of Iowa and sent them a Chinese New Year card extending his festive wishes, continuing the warm exchange of New Year greetings between them for a third consecutive year. Recalling his visit to Iowa 41 years ago, Xi said he was warmly received, and those wonderful memories remain fresh in his mind to this day.
In 1985, Xi, then an official of Zhengding County, Hebei Province in northern China, led a delegation to Iowa. It was Xi's first visit to the United States.
During the trip, he visited Muscatine, a city in rural eastern Iowa, where he stayed with a local family of Thomas and Eleanor Dvorchak. The homestay left a lasting impression.
article_text:
BEIJING, Aug. 8 -- "Friendship stands by a meaningful thing -- a world of peace must be a world of friendship."
Chinese President Xi Jinping once quoted a foreign friend to illustrate the preciousness of friendship. In his view, people-to-people friendship is the foundation for stable and sustained international relations, an inexhaustible driving force for promoting world peace and development and a basic prerequisite for win-win cooperation.
This Spring Festival, Xi replied to friends in the U.S. state of Iowa and sent them a Chinese New Year card extending his festive wishes, continuing the warm exchange of New Year greetings between them for a third consecutive year. Recalling his visit to Iowa 41 years ago, Xi said he was warmly received, and those wonderful memories remain fresh in his mind to this day.
In 1985, Xi, then an official of Zhengding County, Hebei Province in northern China, led a delegation to Iowa. It was Xi's first visit to the United States.
During the trip, he visited Muscatine, a city in rural eastern Iowa, where he stayed with a local family of Thomas and Eleanor Dvorchak. The homestay left a lasting impression.
Recalling the trip decades later, Xi said he still remembered where he stayed: 2911 Bonnie Drive. "That was my first face-to-face contact with the Americans," Xi said. "For me, they represent America."
These old friends reunited in 2023 when Xi visited San Francisco for the APEC leaders' meeting. When Xi saw Gary, son of the Dvorchaks, he said, "I stayed in your room and remember the sweatshirts and ball gear there."
"There was genuine happiness, so you could see the smile on his face. He was really enjoying it," Gary said of the reunion.
Over the past years, Xi added a warmer and more personal touch to Chinese diplomacy by reconnecting with old foreign friends. He has maintained close ties with friends from across the globe through reunions and letters, leaving behind countless warm and heartfelt moments.
In 2014, Xi traveled to Australia's Tasmania to visit the family of his old friend, the late Tasmanian Premier Jim Bacon, honoring a promise he had made years earlier.
Honey Bacon, Bacon's widow, told Xi that her husband had long looked forward to his visit. "Bacon invited me to visit Tasmania then and I agreed. I came here today to fulfill my commitment to him," Xi said.
The two first came to know each other in 1999, when Bacon visited East China's Fujian Province and was received by Xi, then acting governor of the province. They hit it off immediately. Bacon described him as "extraordinary in demeanor," yet as kind and easy-going as an old friend.
In 2001, at Xi's invitation, Bacon led another delegation to Fujian. During the visit, after learning that Bacon was fond of the song "The Waves of Gulangyu," Xi presented a tape of the song as a gift to him. Bacon, in return, invited Xi to "take a walk and have a look" in Tasmania, and Xi gladly accepted the invitation.
However, this turned out to be the last time the two met. Bacon passed away in 2004 after an illness.
During Xi's visit to Tasmania in 2014, Bacon's family showed him photos taken during Bacon's visits to China. Seeing photos of the two of them, Xi said with emotion, "I also keep these photos."
For Xi, friendships like these are never bound by time or distance. He has long attached great importance to people-to-people friendship and closer bonds between peoples, emphasizing that amity between the people holds the key to sound relations between countries, and the people are the cornerstone of the growth of state-to-state relations.
This year marks the 65th anniversary of diplomatic relations between China and Laos, as well as the China-Laos Friendship Year. The China-Laos Railway, a key driver of bilateral trade, economic cooperation and people-to-people exchanges, is also celebrating its fifth year of operation.
Carrying the Lao people's aspiration to transform their country from a landlocked nation into a land-linked hub, the railway stands as a flagship project of the Belt and Road Initiative proposed by Xi. It is also a testament to the enduring friendship and close personal ties cultivated by the leaders of China and Laos over the years.
Sommad Pholsena, who served as the minister of public works and transport of Laos, took part in the construction of the China-Laos Railway. "The Lao people had long dreamed of having a railway," he said. "It was the Belt and Road Initiative that made the China-Laos Railway possible."
Sommad was a schoolmate of Xi. He is the son of the late Quinim Pholsena, a revolutionary leader who was foreign minister of Laos from 1962 to 1963. Several of Pholsena's children lived and studied at Bayi School in Beijing in the 1960s, when Xi was also a student there.
During Xi's visits to Laos in 2010 as Chinese vice president and 2017 as president, he set aside time to meet with his friends from the Pholsena family and reunite with his former schoolmates. "No matter what, I had to make time to see you," Xi told them.
"President Xi is a true friend who values friendship," Sommad said.
He also remembers Xi's words: With the (China-Laos) railway, the mountain from Kunming to Vientiane is no longer high and the road no longer long.
Lasting friendship is built on mutual understanding, respect and sincerity. "Only when people engage each other with sincerity can friendship endure," Xi said. "It is the countless small streams of friendship among peoples that come together to form the mighty force advancing world peace and development and building a community with a shared future for humanity."

title: China upgrades meteorological emergency response, typhoon alert as Typhoon Dolphin approaches
key_facts: BEIJING, Aug. 8 -- China's meteorological authority on Saturday upgraded its emergency response for Typhoon Dolphin to Level III and raised the typhoon warning from yellow to orange as the 13th typhoon of 2026 moves closer to the country's eastern coast.
The China Meteorological Administration upgraded the response from Level IV to Level III, while the National Meteorological Center had earlier upgraded its typhoon warning to orange.

At 9:00 a.m. Saturday, the center of Typhoon Dolphin was located over the southern East China Sea, about 520 km east of Wenzhou in east China's Zhejiang Province, and is forecast to move northwestward at a speed of 10 to 15 km per hour with its intensity remaining stable or slightly strengthening.
The typhoon is expected to make landfall along the coast between Zhoushan in Zhejiang and Fuding in Fujian from Sunday night to Monday morning.

China has a four-tier color-coded weather warning system for typhoons, with red representing the most severe, followed by orange, yellow and blue. It also has a four-tier emergency response system, with Level I being the highest.

title: China activates emergency response for floods as Typhoon Dolphin nears
key_facts: BEIJING, Aug. 7 -- China's Ministry of Water Resources on Friday activated a Level-IV emergency flood response for six provincial regions as the approaching Typhoon Dolphin, the 13th typhoon of 2026, is expected to bring heavy rainfall to east China.

The six regions, namely Shanghai, Jiangsu, Zhejiang, Anhui, Fujian and Jiangxi, all located in east China, will see downpours from Saturday to Wednesday, with several rivers expected to record substantial water level rises, the ministry said.

It has instructed local authorities to strengthen monitoring and research efforts, and manage water projects well in a bid to guard against floods at rivers and reservoirs, as well as the threat of mountain torrents.

The National Meteorological Center (NMC) issued a yellow alert on Friday evening, forecasting Typhoon Dolphin to make landfall along China's eastern coast in either Zhejiang or north Fujian between Sunday afternoon and Monday morning.
Compared with Typhoon Bavi, which made a landfall in the country in July, Typhoon Dolphin may bring stronger winds and heavier rainfall, said Xu Yinglong, chief forecaster at the NMC.

BEIJING, Aug. 7 -- China's Ministry of Water Resources on Friday activated a Level-IV emergency flood response for six provincial regions as the approaching Typhoon Dolphin, the 13th typhoon of 2026, is expected to bring heavy rainfall to east China.
The six regions, namely Shanghai, Jiangsu, Zhejiang, Anhui, Fujian and Jiangxi, all located in east China, will see downpours from Saturday to Wednesday, with several rivers expected to record substantial water level rises, the ministry said.
It has instructed local authorities to strengthen monitoring and research efforts, and manage water projects well in a bid to guard against floods at rivers and reservoirs, as well as the threat of mountain torrents.
The National Meteorological Center (NMC) issued a yellow alert on Friday evening, forecasting Typhoon Dolphin to make landfall along China's eastern coast in either Zhejiang or north Fujian between Sunday afternoon and Monday morning.
Compared with Typhoon Bavi, which made a landfall in the country in July, Typhoon Dolphin may bring stronger winds and heavier rainfall, said Xu Yinglong, chief forecaster at the NMC.
East China and other regions likely to be affected should give priority to typhoon response and take precautions against high winds, rainstorms and secondary disasters, Xu noted.
Also on Friday, the State Flood Control and Drought Relief Headquarters raised its emergency response for flood and typhoon control in Zhejiang and Fujian provinces to Level-III from Level-IV.
A joint consultation involving several central government departments and provincial authorities was held on Friday, urging thorough preparations for the worst by evacuating people from risky areas and stepping up flood control at rivers and lakes, according to the Ministry of Emergency Management.
Typhoon Dolphin could bring extremely heavy rains to eastern, central and northern regions of the country, causing high risks of mountain torrents, geological disasters, flooding of small and medium-sized rivers, and urban waterlogging, the ministry said.
China has a four-tier flood-control emergency response system, with Level I being the most severe.

title: Xiplomacy: Warmth that transcends borders
key_facts: BEIJING, Aug. 7 -- During Russian President Vladimir Putin's China trip this May, Chinese President Xi Jinping invited him to visit a photo exhibition celebrating the everlasting friendship between the two countries at the Great Hall of the People in Beijing.

As the two presidents strolled through the exhibition, viewing pictures documenting their close interactions and the solid progress in China-Russia cooperation, they paused before a familiar image from Moscow's Red Square.

The photograph, taken on May 9, 2025, during celebrations marking the 80th anniversary of the Soviet Union's victory in the Great Patriotic War, showed Xi seated between Putin and Russian World War II veteran Evgeny Znamensky, whose suit was adorned with medals earned through wartime service. The two leaders were seen warmly chatting with the veteran.

Recalling the warm memories of their meeting in Moscow more than a year ago, the 100-year-old veteran said the temperature that day was below 10 degrees Celsius. "President Xi was concerned that I might feel cold and specifically asked for a blanket for me."
Deeply touched by the gesture, Znamensky said he greatly appreciated Xi's kindness.

article_text:
BEIJING, Aug. 7 -- During Russian President Vladimir Putin's China trip this May, Chinese President Xi Jinping invited him to visit a photo exhibition celebrating the everlasting friendship between the two countries at the Great Hall of the People in Beijing.
As the two presidents strolled through the exhibition, viewing pictures documenting their close interactions and the solid progress in China-Russia cooperation, they paused before a familiar image from Moscow's Red Square.
The photograph, taken on May 9, 2025, during celebrations marking the 80th anniversary of the Soviet Union's victory in the Great Patriotic War, showed Xi seated between Putin and Russian World War II veteran Evgeny Znamensky, whose suit was adorned with medals earned through wartime service. The two leaders were seen warmly chatting with the veteran.
Recalling the warm memories of their meeting in Moscow more than a year ago, the 100-year-old veteran said the temperature that day was below 10 degrees Celsius. "President Xi was concerned that I might feel cold and specifically asked for a blanket for me."
Deeply touched by the gesture, Znamensky said he greatly appreciated Xi's kindness.
The blanket was a small gesture, but it speaks volumes about a core tenet of China's diplomacy.
"Friendship, which derives from close contact between the people, holds the key to sound state-to-state relations," Xi articulated this philosophy at the opening ceremony of the Belt and Road Forum for International Cooperation in 2017.
Throughout his overseas visits and diplomatic engagements, Xi has forged friendships with people around the world through sincerity and mutual respect. Even amid a demanding schedule, he has always made time to meet people from all walks of life.
His warm smile and approachable manner have created countless memorable moments, building bridges of mutual understanding and friendship across borders.
During his visit to Russia in May 2015, Xi presented commemorative badges to representatives of Russian veterans to honor their contribution to the victory of the World Anti-Fascist War.
After noticing that the Russian veteran Gaverdovsky was having difficulty walking steadily, Xi told him, "I'll go over and bring the badge to you! You don't need to move." Xi then walked swiftly to Gaverdovsky, and presented the badge to him.
Gaverdovsky said after the ceremony that he was deeply touched by the Chinese president's meticulous care and consideration.
Xi is equally warm and attentive when meeting young people.
In May 2024, Xi paid a state visit to Hungary. Among those greeting the Chinese leader was Hungarian girl Olah Tamara, who had presented flowers to Xi when he visited the country as Chinese vice president in 2009.
After being told that she was the same girl who presented flowers to him 15 years ago, the president recalled that encounter. "You've grown up. You were only this tall back then," he said, making a gesture with his hand.
The brief exchange bridged the years in an instant. Deeply moved, Olah said she had never imagined Xi would still remember her. "He is so warm and kind," she said.
There are many more such moments throughout Xi's overseas visits. Greeting children in Germany on a rainy day, he reminded them to keep warm and avoid catching a cold. In Australia, he set aside time to meet primary school students who had written him letters, invited them to visit China for study tours, and encouraged them to continue writing. Visiting a high school in the U.S. state of Washington, he chatted with students about sports, music and youth.
When meeting workers and farmers, Xi is known for his down-to-earth manner and genuine sincerity.
Having worked and lived alongside farmers in his younger years, Xi has always shared a deep bond with them.
During a visit to a farming family in Costa Rica back in 2013, he reflected on his own experience working in China's countryside, saying he had been a farmer and personally knows what life is like for Chinese farmers.
Walking through the family's small coffee plantation, Xi paused repeatedly to ask the host, Marco Tulio Zamora, about coffee cultivation, production and sales.
For Zamora, the conversation was unforgettable. He said he had rarely seen a foreign leader visit an ordinary family like his, adding that his family felt deeply honored.
During his visit to Serbia in 2016, Xi toured the Smederevo Steel Plant. Inside the vast and bustling hot-rolling workshop, machines roared and heat filled the air. Xi stopped from time to time, closely observing the production process and asking detailed questions about the plant's operations.
Later, Xi visited the staff canteen. What interested him most was the everyday lives of the employees. Nenad Cvetanovic, a veteran employee at the Smederevo Steel Plant, still recalls the sense of encouragement among workers when the Chinese leader told them that the plant would "surely be revitalized."
"President Xi's interaction with us resonated deeply among the workers at the steel plant. His care for us came straight from the heart, giving us a strong sense of security and hope," he said.
Established in 1913, the Smederevo Steel Plant was once regarded as "the pride of Serbia." However, by the late 1990s, declining competitiveness and weak management had pushed the plant to the brink of closure. In 2016, China's HBIS Group acquired the plant. Through joint efforts by both sides, the plant has undergone a breathtaking transformation, regaining its position as one of Serbia's key export drivers.
In 2024, 30 Serbian workers from the steel mill wrote a letter to Xi, sharing the mill's development story and expressing their gratitude for his support in making the project's success possible.
Xi said in his reply letter that it is a great pleasure to learn that the steel plant has turned losses into gains quickly after the investment of a Chinese-funded enterprise.
The development of the plant, he said, cannot be achieved without the dedication and hard work of the workers, who have been working diligently for the quick growth of the steel plant and have written a new chapter for the iron-clad friendship between China and Serbia.
"I give you a thumbs-up," Xi wrote in the letter.

title: China unveils five-year plan for civil aviation industry
key_facts: BEIJING, Aug. 7 -- China's civil aviation regulator on Friday released a development plan for the civil aviation industry during the 2026-2030 period.

According to the plan issued by the Civil Aviation Administration of China (CAAC), the industry aims to achieve world-class standards in safety, service capacity and infrastructure by 2030, while securing major breakthroughs in technological innovation, green and low-carbon development, and governance capacity.

By then, the industry will provide stronger support for major national strategies, boost regional economic and social development, and better meet people's needs for air travel, according to the plan.
To achieve these goals, the industry will pursue smart, green and integrated development during the 2026-2030 period, with safety as the bottom line, the plan notes.

The Piraeus Port project is one example of Xi's close attention to cooperation projects such as the Jakarta-Bandung High-Speed Railway and Chancay Port in Peru, which bring tangible benefits to local communities.
For Xi, the true value of cooperation is measured not only by economic gains, but also by how it improves people's lives.
During his visit to Tajikistan in September 2014, Xi attended a ceremony marking the commencement of a China-Tajikistan joint thermal power plant in Dushanbe. Seeing the difficulties faced by local people due to shortages of electricity and heating, Xi said he had experienced hardship himself and could empathize with them. Projects truly benefiting local people were the best ones, he added.
As Xi has said, "Development is real only when all countries develop together. Prosperity and stability cannot be possible in a world where the rich become richer while the poor are made poorer. Every nation aspires for a better life, and modernization is not a privilege reserved for any single country."
Xi's vision of common progress is taking root in regions like Africa, where countries are striving for faster development.
In 2013, Xi chose Africa for his first overseas visit after assuming the presidency. During the visit, he put forward the principles of China's Africa policy -- sincerity, real results, amity and good faith, and pursuing the greater good and shared interests.
In his keynote address at the opening ceremony of the 2024 Beijing Summit of the Forum on China-Africa Cooperation, Xi said that "on the path to modernization, no one, and no country, should be left behind."
Over the years, China-Africa cooperation has expanded beyond economic sectors into areas closely related to people's livelihoods. In Kenya, the Mombasa-Nairobi Standard Gauge Railway has become a major transport link in East Africa, while China-supported water projects have helped millions of African people gain access to safe drinking water.
Cooperation has also extended to the public health sector, with the Africa Centres for Disease Control and Prevention headquarters, built with Chinese support, helping strengthen health capacity across the continent. This May, China further opened its market wider to African countries by fully implementing zero-tariff treatment to all 53 African countries with which it maintains diplomatic relations.
"The greatest good in China-Africa relations is to closely combine Africa's independent and sustainable development with China's own development," Xi said. "The ultimate goal is to realize win-win cooperation."
One example is Juncao technology, which Xi promoted while working in east China's Fujian Province more than two decades ago. He later introduced the technology to a visiting official from Papua New Guinea, paving the way for its overseas application.
Juncao technology, which uses a type of grass to cultivate edible mushrooms, feed livestock and prevent soil erosion, has become an effective tool for poverty reduction and sustainable development.
"I did go to Fujian Province. I met my then colleague, Governor Xi Jinping," said Peti Lafanama, former governor of Papua New Guinea's Eastern Highlands Province. "I think the President has a heart for the people."
The vision of building a community with a shared future for humanity is also reflected in Xi's efforts in global climate governance. Xi has repeatedly called for global solidarity to address this pressing challenge, stressing that ecological protection concerns the well-being and future of all countries.
China played "a decisive role" in the negotiation process of the Paris Agreement in December 2015, said former UN Secretary-General Ban Ki-moon, expressing his gratitude for China's contribution to accelerating the ratification process of the agreement.
"Had not been President Xi Jinping's initiative, we would not have the Paris Agreement on climate change even now," said Ban.
In 2025, the 10th anniversary of the Paris Agreement, Xi announced China's 2035 Nationally Determined Contributions at the UN Climate Summit, a move that further demonstrated China's commitment and determination to advancing global green development.
"These targets represent China's best efforts based on the requirements of the Paris Agreement," Xi said in his video remarks to the UN summit.
Through years of active participation in global climate governance and efforts to inspire younger generations to protect the planet, Xi has also called for building a community of all life on Earth in a bid to promote sustainable development for humanity.
"Our people hope to successfully realize national development, but they also hope to see all peoples of the world leading happy and peaceful lives," Xi has said.

title: Reading seminar on Xi's book on governance held in Tajikistan
key_facts: DUSHANBE, Aug. 6 -- A reading seminar on the fifth volume of "Xi Jinping: The Governance of China" was held Wednesday here in the capital of Tajikistan.
Participants from various sectors of China and Tajikistan shared their reflections on the book and exchanged views on Chinese modernization and China-Tajikistan relations.

The event, themed "Advancing Modernization Together and Building a China-Tajikistan Community with a Shared Future," was jointly organized by China International Communications Group, the Chinese Embassy in Tajikistan and the Dipservice under the Tajik Foreign Ministry.

Chinese Ambassador to Tajikistan Guo Zhijun said the book not only documents China's development practices, but also contains profound reflections on state governance, social development, people's well-being and international cooperation.

Its publication will help the international community keep abreast of the latest development of Xi Jinping Thought on Socialism with Chinese Characteristics for a New Era and deepen its understanding of China's ideas, solutions and wisdom, Guo said.

Its publication will help the international community keep abreast of the latest development of Xi Jinping Thought on Socialism with Chinese Characteristics for a New Era and deepen its understanding of China's ideas, solutions and wisdom, Guo said.
Rashid Alimov, former secretary-general of the Shanghai Cooperation Organization and professor at the Academy of Public Administration under the President of Tajikistan, said the ideas presented in the book have been validated both in theory and through China's development practices.
China's historic eradication of extreme poverty, its emergence as a major global economy and its growing role in scientific and technological innovation demonstrate the vitality of these ideas, he said.
In a video address, Yang Jin, deputy director of the Center for Central Asia and the Caucasus Studies at the Institute of Russian, Eastern European and Central Asian Studies under the Chinese Academy of Social Sciences, said Chinese modernization is a successful path suited to China's national conditions.
It is also a path of peaceful development, openness and mutually beneficial cooperation, creating broader space for aligning the development strategies of China and Tajikistan, Yang said.
The book also inspired Anora Nazhmuddinova, a Chinese-language major in Dushanbe who is preparing to study in Shanghai.
She said the book contains rich ideas on cooperation and development and calls on countries to pursue common development and mutual benefit. She hopes to continue drawing inspiration from it and become a young ambassador for China-Tajikistan friendship.

title: Xiplomacy: Hosting the world, building the future
key_facts: BEIJING, Aug. 6 -- As southern China's metropolis of Shenzhen prepares to host the 33rd Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation Economic Leaders' Meeting in November, China is once again extending its welcoming arms to leaders from around the world.

article_text:
BEIJING, Aug. 6 -- As southern China's metropolis of Shenzhen prepares to host the 33rd Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation Economic Leaders' Meeting in November, China is once again extending its welcoming arms to leaders from around the world.
Over the years, China has hosted a series of major diplomatic gatherings that have brought together world leaders. More than simply platforms for dialogue, these occasions have showcased China's vision for global cooperation and offered a glimpse of President Xi Jinping's approach to diplomacy.
For Xi, hosting world leaders begins with hospitality.
In May 2023, on his 70th birthday, Kazakh President Kassym-Jomart Tokayev arrived in the ancient Silk Road city of Xi'an for a state visit to China and the inaugural China-Central Asia Summit. During their talks, Xi extended birthday wishes to his guest.
"On this special occasion, your visit speaks volumes about the strength of our bilateral ties and reaffirms your unique bond with China," Xi said with a smile.
"Thank you," Tokayev, who speaks fluent Mandarin, replied in Chinese.
An old Chinese saying goes: "Is it not a real delight to have friends coming to visit you from afar?"
Whether welcoming old friends or first-time visitors, Xi's attentiveness has become a defining feature of China's diplomacy as a host, helping foster mutual trust and friendship.
Yet these gatherings are about more than hospitality.
In times of global uncertainty, they have also served as venues where China has called for dialogue, openness and cooperation while presenting its proposals to address shared challenges.
In 2016, China hosted the Group of 20 (G20) summit for the first time. Chaired by Xi, the summit marked a milestone in global economic governance.
At the summit, development was placed at the forefront of the global macro-policy agenda for the first time. The summit, which brought together a record number of developing countries, also witnessed the adoption of an action plan to advance the implementation of the UN 2030 Agenda for Sustainable Development, as well as the first-ever collective commitment to support industrialization in Africa and the least developed countries.
These initiatives, together with the summit's outcome documents, reflected China's commitment to common development and shared prosperity.
As today's world is struggling with mounting conflicts, as well as the rise of hegemonism, protectionism and other global challenges, Xi has chosen a series of major diplomatic events hosted by China to put forward his key proposals.
The Global Security Initiative was unveiled at the Boao Forum for Asia in 2022, followed by the Global Civilization Initiative at the Communist Party of China in Dialogue with World Political Parties High-level Meeting in 2023, the Global Governance Initiative at the Shanghai Cooperation Organization (SCO) Tianjin Summit last year, and a renewed call to implement the Global Development Initiative at the conference marking the 70th anniversary of the Five Principles of Peaceful Coexistence in 2024.
These proposals have been backed by concrete actions. Behind every summit lies an intensive diplomatic schedule personally led by Xi.
On Sept. 2, 2018, ahead of the opening of the Beijing Summit of the Forum on China-Africa Cooperation (FOCAC), Xi held 11 bilateral meetings with African leaders, with every engagement timed to the minute.
At the G20 Hangzhou Summit in 2016, Xi attended 13 meetings and various events within just over 80 hours, during which he delivered 11 speeches, and met with 27 foreign leaders. At the SCO Qingdao Summit in 2018, he participated in more than 20 official events in two days.
The tightly packed schedule underscores not only the intensity of China's diplomatic engagement, but also Xi's personal commitment to advancing international dialogue and cooperation.
China has sought not only to put forward ideas, but also to turn them into action.
Since the Belt and Road Initiative was launched in 2013, it has generated nearly 1 trillion U.S. dollars in global investment and created at least 500,000 jobs in partner countries. In Africa and many other parts of the world, the thriving Belt and Road cooperation has been widely considered a road to prosperity.
Following the successful implementation of the Ten Cooperation Plans, the Eight Major Initiatives and the Nine Programs, Xi announced a new positioning of China-Africa relations and 10 partnership actions at the 2024 FOCAC Beijing Summit, opening a new chapter in the joint pursuit of modernization.
Over the years, the major diplomatic events hosted by China have marked a journey, along which China and the rest of the world have moved forward together.
As China welcomes the world to Shenzhen, it also renews its commitment to working with countries around the world to build broader consensus on peace and development, strengthen openness and cooperation, and open a new chapter in building a community with a shared future for humanity.

title: China, Argentina renew currency swap agreement
key_facts: BEIJING, Aug. 6 -- The People's Bank of China (PBOC), the country's central bank, said Thursday that it has renewed a bilateral currency swap agreement with the Central Bank of Argentina.
The swap amount is set at 130 billion yuan (about 19.1 billion U.S. dollars), equivalent to 28 trillion Argentine pesos, according to the PBOC.
The agreement runs for five years and is renewable by mutual consent, the PBOC noted.

The renewal of the bilateral currency swap agreement will help further deepen financial cooperation between the two countries, facilitate bilateral economic and trade exchanges, and safeguard financial market stability, the PBOC said.

title: China completes new geologic map of Moon
key_facts: BEIJING, Aug. 6 -- A Chinese research team has completed an updated geologic map of the entire Moon on a scale of 1:5 million, said the Institute of Geology, Chinese Academy of Geological Sciences on Thursday.

The main map, about 280 cm long and 120 cm high, comes with inset geologic maps of the Moon's polar regions. It precisely marks over 13,000 impact craters and 81 impact basins, and delineates 14 types of geological structures and 17 types of rocks.

Drawing on the latest findings from China's Chang'e lunar exploration program and other lunar research, the map introduces systematic updates to the lunar geological time scale, lunar material classification and the cartographic presentation of geologic features.

The team revised the lunar geological time scale, setting the beginnings of the Aitkenian, Nectarian and Imbrian periods at 4.33 billion, 4.17 billion and 3.92 billion years ago, respectively. For the first time globally, the map provides a finer subdivision of stratigraphic units representing the later stages of the Moon's geologic history.

The map also incorporates higher-resolution data showing the distribution of key minerals on the lunar surface and refines the rock classification system. Drawing on the latest findings from the Chang'e-4 and Chang'e-6 missions, it adds gabbronorite as a distinct rock type in the South Pole-Aitken (SPA) Basin.

BEIJING, Aug. 6 -- A Chinese research team has completed an updated geologic map of the entire Moon on a scale of 1:5 million, said the Institute of Geology, Chinese Academy of Geological Sciences on Thursday.
The main map, about 280 cm long and 120 cm high, comes with inset geologic maps of the Moon's polar regions. It precisely marks over 13,000 impact craters and 81 impact basins, and delineates 14 types of geological structures and 17 types of rocks.

The team revised the lunar geological time scale, setting the beginnings of the Aitkenian, Nectarian and Imbrian periods at 4.33 billion, 4.17 billion and 3.92 billion years ago, respectively. For the first time globally, the map provides a finer subdivision of stratigraphic units representing the later stages of the Moon's geologic history.
The map also incorporates higher-resolution data showing the distribution of key minerals on the lunar surface and refines the rock classification system. Drawing on the latest findings from the Chang'e-4 and Chang'e-6 missions, it adds gabbronorite as a distinct rock type in the South Pole-Aitken (SPA) Basin.
For the 1:5 million scale, the team set different minimum mapping thresholds by feature category, preserving overall legibility without omitting geologic details of major scientific value.
China released the world's first geologic map of the Moon on a scale of 1:2,500,000 in 2022, and published the world's first complete high-definition lunar geologic atlas in 2024.
The new map provides scientific support for the construction of China's future lunar research station, landing site selection and deep-space exploration, said Yang Zhiming, director of the institute, adding that this represents a fresh Chinese contribution to humanity's exploration of the evolution of the solar system.

title: China maintains Level-IV emergency flood response for Shaanxi, Heilongjiang
key_facts: BEIJING, Aug. 6 -- The Ministry of Water Resources has kept a Level-IV emergency flood response in place for both Shaanxi Province in northwest China and Heilongjiang Province in the northeast, the ministry said Thursday.

Five working groups dispatched by the ministry are assisting and guiding on-site flood prevention and control efforts in Heilongjiang, Inner Mongolia Autonomous Region in north China and south China's Hainan Province, among other regions.
From Wednesday morning to Thursday morning, rainfall pushed 15 rivers in Shaanxi and southwest China's Yunnan Province above warning levels.
The ministry urged local authorities to step up safety measures for reservoirs and check dams, bolster flood defenses along small and medium-sized rivers, and guard against flash floods.
China has a four-tier flood-control emergency response system, with Level I being the most severe.

title: China allocates 330 mln yuan from central relief fund to 8 flood-hit provinces
key_facts: BEIJING, Aug. 5 -- China's Ministry of Finance and its Ministry of Emergency Management on Wednesday allocated 330 million yuan (about 48.61 million U.S. dollars) from the central natural disaster relief fund to eight provincial-level regions impacted by flooding.
They are Heilongjiang, Liaoning and Jilin, all in the northeast, Chongqing, Sichuan, Guizhou and Yunnan in the southwest, and Shaanxi in northwest China.

With China experiencing its main flood season from late July to early August, vast swathes of the country have been hit by persistent heavy rainfall, triggering floods and geological disasters that have caused casualties and left homes damaged or destroyed.

The funds are designated for emergency rescue and relief operations, with a focus on search and rescue, relocation and resettlement of affected people, emergency response, hazard removal and risk reduction, inspection and rectification of secondary disaster risks, and repair of damaged homes, with all aimed at minimizing disaster losses as much as possible.
